capabilities: Show random vault notes one at a time through a floating button bar
Run spaced repetition flashcards with Wrong/Hard/Correct/Easy grading and FSRS-based intervals
Prompt recurring habits and self check-in questions
Feed one-time to-dos into the queue
Support iterative reading of short and long media with limits on concurrent long items
extras: The author states they are "currently not actively working on this project", though it remains available and a roadmap is promised. Documentation covers The Queue 2, a rewrite, with old documentation linked separately. The README repeatedly warns that habit and mental-health check-in notes cannot replace professional help. Detailed local-development instructions are still pending.
motivation: The author opens the README with "There is no point in creating notes you never see again!", framing the plugin as the culmination of years of tinkering with spaced repetition and note-taking methods.
problem: Notes written once tend to be forgotten; Obsidian has no built-in way to resurface notes for spaced repetition, habit tracking, or gradual reading.

relations.evidence: The folder settings' code is inspired by Templater, which in turn credits Liam's Periodic Notes Plugin
ebisu, the algorithm that flashcards used to be based on.

summary: Random-review queue that resurfaces vault notes one at a time as flashcards, habits, check-ins, to-dos, or reading prompts via a floating button bar.
